transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2026-02-07 13:00 PT (Recorded)
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Aisha (Redwood AE), Marco (Redwood SE), Tanya (Redwood CSM), Liam (Quantivio CTO), Priya (Infra), Daniel (SRE), Marta (Security)

Summary: quick weekly checkin for the Quantivio Private POC focusing on a recent staging egress spike, fallback routing behavior, and a proposed kernel rollback to address outlier latency.
Topics: staging egress surge, VPC egress rules / NAT, fallback routing behavior, kernel/kv cache rollback, telemetry gaps, next steps for prod cutover

[00:00] Aisha: hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick agenda — we wanted to walk through the egress surge you saw last night, share the SE findings, and align on the rollback plan and next benchmark.
[00:22] Liam: yeah thanks aisha. hit pretty high egress at 01:13 UTC, saw many flows to our third-party spam-filter and to S3, plus a surge of long context requests. wondering if this is the batch behaviour you mentioned.
[00:45] Marco: ok, so from Redwood side we replayed the logs — looks like a change in the request distribution: token sequence lengths spiked and triggered continuous batching to increase batch depth, that combined with prefix cache misses created transient egress bursts. also saw a couple of retries due to our internal circuit breaker, so extra downstream calls.
[01:12] Priya: we saw the same, and our NAT gateway hit the connection limit for a few minutes which then started queuing, causing connection churn. we had to bump ephemeral NAT ports.
[01:40] Marco: that matches. on the runtime trace we also saw a hot shard where KV cash (note: transcribed as "KV cash") wasn't hitting as expected for a specific model variant; that pushed more compute requests and more egress.
[02:05] Daniel: there were constant TLS handshakes during the spike — roughly 8k new TLS connections over 3 minutes, which is abnormal for our steady state. how is connection reuse/keepalive handled?
[02:28] Marco: keepalive is negotiated by the client/proxy, but in the private pack we have options for long-lived multiplexed connections. looks like your proxies were opening short-lived connections which prevented reuse.
[02:50] Liam: should we be routing through the Redwood egress proxy or use our own? we had thought the proxy would reduce handshake load.
[03:12] Aisha: good question — for staging we recommended using Quantivio's proxy for logging reasons, but for prod the recommended pattern is a single egress NAT with mTLS to Redwood to reduce handshake churn.
[03:35] Marta: security here — we need to ensure mTLS and KMS access patterns are preserved. if there is a fallback to hosted, we need audit logs and key access controls.
[03:58] Tanya: quick note — we'll include the audit log excerpt in the package we send.
[04:20] Marco: back to the technical — we proposed two mitigations: 1) tune batching thresholds so the runtime doesn't aggressively increase batch depth on short spikes, 2) enable prefix-KV prefetch for the 768-token window that our clients use most. the first provides immediate relief, second reduces backend fetches.
[04:55] Priya: can you scope the impact of changing batching thresholds? curious about latency tradeoffs.
[05:12] Marco: yes, lowering max-batch-depth will reduce throughput but cap the egress spike; we're seeing in internal sims a 15-25% latency improvement for P95 during spikes, with a 5-7% cost increase per token in steady state if applied globally. we can apply it as a canary for the staging cluster only.
[05:40] Liam: and what about kernel rollback — you mentioned that earlier in the channel.
[05:55] Marco: right. last week we rolled a kernel micro-optimization that changed kernel selection heuristics; it reduced tail lat for some models but had a regression in cache warmth for others. we have a rollback package that restores previous kernel selection and KV cache management. on staging it reduces these cache-miss-induced egress bursts in our internal tests.
[06:25] Daniel: how long is the rollback window — is it quick to flip back? we need a safe rollback path if something else breaks.
[06:40] Marco: we've baked an automated rollback tag that takes ~4–7 minutes to reimage the inference nodes in the staging pool; the SE runbook includes health checks and traffic drain. we'll share the runbook.
[06:58] Priya: downtime? will requests drop while reimaging?
[07:10] Marco: no planned downtime for canary; we'll route traffic away from nodes during the change. there may be transient latency for requests that hit the rolling nodes but no broad outage.
[07:30] Liam: ok, good. security question: if you push the rollback, will it change TLS certs or KMS access?
[07:45] Marco: no cert changes. KMS interactions unchanged. only kernel-level heuristics.
[08:05] Marta: we need the list of exact config toggles you plan to change so we can get it through our change control.
[08:18] Aisha: noted — marco will share a config diff and a one-page change control summary.
[08:30] Tanya: also, we'll bundle the SOC2 excerpt and the telemetry mapping so you can map logs to your SIEM.
[08:45] Daniel: on telemetry — we noticed some missing request IDs in traces during the spike. that makes root cause harder. can you confirm the SDK is propogating IDs?
[09:02] Marco: there was a bug in the SDK edge-case where request IDs weren't added for batched multiplexed requests when client included a pre-signed header. it's fixed in the patch we're about to promote.
[09:20] Priya: great — timeline for that promotion?
[09:28] Marco: we can push the telemetry fix and kernel rollback as part of the same staging patch tomorrow (2026-02-08) evening UTC, subject to your change window.
[09:40] Liam: do we have a tentative benchmark after the patch?
[09:52] Aisha: yes we proposed Thu 2026-02-12 for a full 1M-token stress run with both steady and spiky distributions. marco will run parallel runs with and without rollback to compare.
[10:10] Daniel: what about egress filtering? we want to whitelist exact endpoints and ports so our NAT isn't surprised.
[10:25] Marco: please send the final egress CIDR + port list — we'll confirm the IPs Redwood will call out to and provide a validated list.
[10:42] Priya: also, what about connection pooling — is there a recommended proxy config? our envoy upstream had idle timeouts at 10s, maybe that's too low.
[10:58] Marco: recommended upstream idle ~120s for long lived connections to allow keepalive reuse; that drastically cuts TLS handshakes. we'll send an example envoy config.
[11:20] Liam: simultaneous question — cost. if we cap batching, cost per token may go up; we need a runway number for the peak month.
[11:37] Aisha: we'll add estimated unit economics for the canary change in the follow-up email — approximate percent change and monthly delta for your projected load.
[11:50] Marta: compliance — if you fallback to hosted for some tenants, we need to confirm data residency and KMS separation. will fallback honor separate key namespaces?
[12:07] Marco: fallback will use dedicated tenant keys if requested; for the POC you have dedicated KMS namespaces still controlled by Quantivio keys in HSM. we'll document the fallback key behavior.
[12:30] Priya: curious about the telemetry gaps you mentioned earlier — will these be fixed in the same patch?
[12:40] Marco: yes telemetry ID propagation and the SDK header bug are in the same commit planned for staging tomorrow.
[12:55] Daniel: re: NAT port exhaustion — will Redwood throttle connections on your side or should we set up our proxy to queue?
[13:10] Marco: better to queue at your proxy; Redwood throttles at the route level but that will generate retries that increase egress. If your proxy holds and multiplexes we avoid extra upstream calls.
[13:30] Liam: ok, for prod cutover we want a checklist. can you draft a cutover checklist covering egress rules, idle timeouts, rollout canary steps, rollback runbook, and audit evidence?
[13:45] Aisha: absolutely — that will be in the follow-up.
[14:00] Tanya: before we close, quick recap of commitments and owners.
[14:10] Aisha: recap — marco will push patch to staging (telemetry fix + kernel rollback) on 2026-02-08, share runbook and config diff; aisha to send SOC2 excerpt and network diagram by 2026-02-10; daniel to provide final egress CIDRs by 2026-02-08; marta to review KMS rotation notes by 2026-02-14; benchmark scheduled 2026-02-12.
[14:40] Liam: sounds good, thanks. one last minor note — we saw a tiny discrepancy in per-route token accounting in the console; can we get a token-per-route breakdown export?
[15:00] Tanya: yes will include the export.
[15:10] Marta: thanks everyone.
[15:20] Meeting closed.
